sentences.text: % 19.09.2023 [The proceeding has been conducted through Hybrid mode]
1. Mr. Chocksey, learned counsel appearing for the applicant submits that FIR in the instance case was registered on 14.08.2022 under Section 376 IPC r/w Sections 4/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

2. Learned counsel invites attention of this Court to the allegations contained in the FIR to submit that the same allegations have been made in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., 1973 by the victim, however, in contradistinction to the same, statement recorded before learned MM under Section 164 Cr.P.C does not disclose any details of what were referred to by the victim in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C or as recorded in the FIR or even in the chargesheet.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the FIR, the assailant is named as Ranjan.
In the Statement under Section 164 This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 26/09/2023 at 20:50:46 Cr.P.C recorded before the learned MM, victim refers to assailant as Ravi.
Learned counsel submits that the applicant in the present case is neither Ranjan or Ravi and his actual name is Mohd Rafi.

On that basis, learned counsel submits that there is whole lot of doubt on the identity of the applicant himself and thus the applicant should be released on bail on that ground.
4.
Learned counsel further submits that in present case the chargesheet has been filed.

That apart,
the child/victim has already been examined, cross-examined and discharged.
Accordingly, learned counsel for the applicant states that only that the father of the victim is yet to be cross-examined.

sentences.text: However, he further submits that the father of the victim is admittedly a resident of Jharkhand even at the time of the alleged incident and thus his statement may not hold much water so far as the case of the prosecution is concerned.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant also submits that the applicant is a young man of 21 years and of impressionable age and therefore to detain him in judicial custody along with other hardened criminal may not be justified in the facts of the present case.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the applicant has been incarceration from 15.08.2022 onwards without any interim bail till today.

8. Mr. Mukesh Kumar, learned APP for the State submits that the father of the victim is to be examined on 22.09.2023 and requests that the present bail application be taken for consideration subsequent thereto.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 26/09/2023 at 20:50:46 9.
Keeping in view the fact that the father of the victim is yet to be examined, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application may be taken for consideration soon thereafter.
10. Accordingly, re-notify on 28.11.2023.
11. Victim is present in person.
Learned APP for the State submits that the victim has to travel from Jharkhand every time to appear before this court.
It may not be easy for her to come and attend this Court personally.
12. Keeping in view the aforesaid submissions made by the learned APP for the State, the victim is exempted from personal appearance and unless her presence is required, she need not appear.
TUSHAR RAO GEDELA, J SEPTEMBER 19, 2023/at
